item.description: Do you guys know about any obscure but good SCP games?
item.content:encoded:
I first got into SCP because one of my friends wanted me to play Secret Lab with him (a game I know love and think is a little underrated). I’ve played pretty much all of the popular ones like CB, SCP Unity, SCP 087, SCP Terminal, and Fractured Minds. I think I might’ve played a few others. I was wondering if any of you guys know about any hidden gems (though I don’t expect anyone to), because I really like most of the SCP games that I’ve played before (even though they may not be a accurate portrayal of the modern SCP website, they’re still fun so please don’t bully) and was wondering if there’s anything left.

item.title: Flashpoint Just league Dark
item.content:encoded:
So I’ve seen parts of Justice League Dark Apokolips (which was, a bit to dark for me.) but I know Barry travels back in time to try and change stuff but I’m not clear whether this actually resets things, or just creates an alternate timeline.
I would like it to reset because honestly, maybe I’m too soft or super edge brutal killing isn’t me, but I hope it’s a reset. I just couldn’t really like seeing characters I’ve loved for years die so indignantly. Starfire was the one that definitely made me cringe, Grayson and her built up something and she’s mechanized after being torn in two. And I like the previous movies, but this was too much for me. Call me queezy, I have a threshold for dark. Especially when it comes to beloved characters. MK they always die gruesomely so that never bothers me. So I want more movies but with the reset.

item.title: SCP Foundation? What SCP Foundatin? This is the PCS Foundation!
item.description: A discussion on how to create a universe where anomalous objects and an organization captures them and research them.
item.content:encoded:
Hello Hello! This is just a general thought that I have in my mind.

We all love our wonderful SCP Foundation universe. We love the way the system work and the anomalous objects. So much so that we can potentially recognize those same things in this other works.

There is this piece of media (I won't say the name but you can guess) that came out in 2019. It's about a world where anomalous objects exist and there is an American organization that is dedicating to capturing these objects and researching them. In this universe, this organization takes place in a building that mysteriously appeared a long time ago and looks super creepy.

+ show block
– hide block

Now when this game came out, a lot of people made comparisons to the SCP Foundation. Rightly so, as it did borrow a few things from the SCP universe. For example, there are several objects that are just ordinary but have weird qualities to them (There is a fridge that you have to stare at or else it starts to kill people). There is also an overwhelming sense of bureaucracy with files upon files of information related to any anomalous object of note.

So here comes the question, is it possible to create a universe where anomalous objects exist there is an organization (or several organizations) that seek to capture them and research them while being distinct from the SCP Universe?

Feel free to discuss this in the thread but I would like to throw in my own two cents. I think the best thing you can do when it comes to making sure your universe is distinct from the SCP universe is clarity and specifics. So much of the SCP Universe is shrouded in mystery. While there are a lot of concrete specific definitions for there specific things (Clearance Levels, Mobile Task Forces, etc) there is still a lot of mystery. If you read the O5 Command Dossier, you don't see descriptions for one person who is specifically labeled O5-X, you see an entire list of people who could potentially be O5-X. Hell, you can see a note saying that the O5 council might not be real.

When I say that clarity and specifics can be used for distinction, what I mean is that you can have a lot of explanations and worldbuilding in your universe. How did these objects come to be? Why are they like that? Are there multiple reasons why or is there just one big reason why? How did the world react to them? Do people like these objects or not? All of these standard worldbuilding questions can be used to make your world feel more different from the SCP Universe. Specifics and clarity make your idea yours.

It also helps not to straight-up steal concepts from the website. I know that might seem kinda hard since there is so much content on the site (5000+ entries and so on), you might accidentally rip off someone but as someone who has an entire list of SCP ideas on a Google Doc and who also see's which ideas have been done before (Spoiler alert, a lot of them haven't been done yet), I think it is much easier to make an idea and add specifics to that idea in order to make it your idea than to just take something wholesale from the site. Especially if you are just stealing from the Hall of Fame section.

What do you guys think? Feel free to discuss this!


As a courtesy to our readers on mobile devices, please collapse long posts. ~Zyn

item.title: In The Balance | An SCP-inspired creative in the works
item.description: In The Balance is going to be a creative made by Affray Studios that will not be a part of the SCP Wiki. It will be used primarily in games and short film projects to avoid licensing risk and to give us more creative freedom.
item.content:encoded:
Concept logo

+ show block
– hide block

In The Balance is going to be a creative made by Affray Studios that will not be a part of the SCP Wiki. It will be used primarily in games and short film projects to avoid licensing risk and to give us and potential partners more creative freedom.

This creation is not intended to directly rival with the wiki or anything alike, this is purely an option we are creating so that we and other creators can have a new option to work with projects we need more control over. This can be as simple as getting proper publishing/investor agreements and deals, potentially getting onto curated video streaming platforms such as Netflix, and so on.

Along with the "why", we really like the idea of the SCP Foundation and other organizations made for this creative. This is why we are keeping similar themes while being able to make this our own standalone property.

There will be no directly derived content from the wiki under this that is heavily unique to this platform. That would be incredibly ████. It's unavoidable to have similar ideas or accidentally create something based on our memory of the wiki, but we will not infringe on any creators' unique work. An example I give is that we won't have a plague doctor that wants to "cure" people, but we may have something fairly more generic like blind quadrupedal creators. And even in the event of similar concepts, the specific characteristics will almost never be the same.

If we ever do stumble into uncomfortable territory for any creators our email will always be open. This is also open to anyone with questions, concerns, interest in collaboration, and so on. Truly email us for anything you want to talk to us for - note that I may not be able to see replies to this post.

In The Balance: Faultline | Game by Affray Studios

Colapsed for long forum post:

+ show block
– hide block

And as some of you may know, we were originally working on an overly-ambitious project known as "SCP: Ascension". We have since rebranded a lot of our ideas for SCP:A under "In The Balance" and have started to refund the pledges on our original Kickstarter for those who request it after our announcement on the matter.

Our upcoming project after SCP: Pandemic (unrelated to COVID-19, just unfortunate timing) will be In The Balance: Faultline, which will derive from our once-plans for SCP:A's Blackout and Recon with some modification for this universe. The gamemodes are now (in order) Downfall and Blackout.

Faultline's Downfall will take place in Contract Recovery Sectors, which are areas affected by extranormal entities or the human response to them. These areas often include fallen black sites once housing containment and research, in which private companies are contracted to raid in order to recover information, items, and caches. Other companies will be actively competing against you as you take the contracts on - arm yourself appropriately.

Faultlines's Blackout will be slightly more traditional in the eyes of the SCP community, it will be about forces responding to active containment breaches. A more fledged out plan will be released once we've been able to start Downfall in the near future. Development of In The Balance: Faultline is planned for late 2020 to early 2021.

Film-related projects

We currently plan to take on virtual production & live-action with a few members of Affray and various partners. More information on this will be released at a later time. Feel free to get in contact with us if you have any interest or suggestions. Truly.

Game projects

We also desire to open up In The Balance long-term to other development teams for their own projects.

item.title: A Really Weird Dream
item.description: Just something I wanted to talk about
item.content:encoded:
I think this post might be a bit on the longer end. So, if you're easily bored, I recommend picking something else to read.

+ show block
– hide block

I just woke up from a nap, and it's had to be the weirdest dream in my life. I fell asleep on top of my chemistry homework, and the last thing I remember crossing my mind before nodding off was Astral Projection. I don't know why I was thinking about it. All I remember was just imagining floating, and just sort of feeling like my limbs were flailing around, even though I knew my body wasn't moving. And then, the next thing I knew, I was awake (I was still dreaming, of course). I was still in the same spot I had fallen asleep in, except it was early daytime instead of late afternoon (the time that I'd fallen asleep). I knew because there were birds singing, and the sun outside was a lot brighter than when I fell asleep. Anyways, I opened my bedroom blinds to let in the light, and I just see this giant cat's face staring at me. It wasn't a normal cat though. It was more like if someone crossed cheshire cat, momo, and grumpy cat, then blew it up to about twenty times the initial size. And it was just staring at me through the window. Obviously, I flip out, I go to tell my parents, but they're busy arguing about something…I have no idea what, and they don't normally argue. But they kept shushing me when I tried telling them about the cat.

I tried going outside to my house into my backyard to see the cat, but I think it attacks me or looks at me or something. But then I'm suddenly tumbling down a hillside, and my head crashes into something, then I get knocked out. I wake up again, and I'm in the same exact place in my room. I re-open the window, same chesire cat, same freakout, same tumbling down a hill, and repeat for about five times. And the weirdest thing is, even though I know I'm 100% awake right now, I can still feel my forehead throbbing from smacking against…something. I don't know what. I was out gardening earlier today, so something might have hit me then. My head doesn't hurt or anything…it just fields weird.

But fifth time proves to be the charm, and when I go outside, the cat doesn't attack me. It just looks at me. I then see that it's on my neighbor's property instead of my own property. Somehow, I get my school counselor (don't ask me WHY he ended up in my dream) to come look at the cat, and he agrees that it's creepy and that it shouldn't be there. I don't see the cat for most of the dream, so that's a plus.

Then I go driving with my dad to go pick up flowers from a family friend's garden. (Okay, so note this is something that happened earlier today. I was trying to start a butterfly garden in my back yard, and we had a family friend that lives about 20 minutes away, so me and my dad actually drove to her house today to pick up the plants.) And that's when things start getting really weird. The sky somehow turns bloodred, like the sun is setting, except the sun is still high in the sky. And when we're driving, we drive past all these machines, which I'm pretty sure were grinders. We also drive through a city called which I think was called Greensboro. My dad tells me to remember Greensboro, because "Greensboro is where everything happens". We finally arrive at the family friend's house, and she seems normal enough. But the plants are just really off. The flowers are all the wrong colors. And they just looked off. I'm not sure how to describe them. They just looked weird. But nonetheless, we took them.

And then I remember falling again. The same tumbling sensation I had with the chesire cat. And then I woke up again, except I was driving on the freeway. It was pitch-black, with the exception of my headlights lighting up the bumper of this white jeep in front of me. I could see the back of the head of the man n the front, and he seemed slumped over. I almost crash into him about 5 times, and I have a major panic attack every time I do. My dad isn't with me in the car. (I'm a minor, and I'm not allowed to drive by myself.) But every time I get too close to the car, he just appears in the backseat behind me and begins screeching at me. I think he even tried to choke me or hurt me in some way. (My dad is extremely kind and nice to me. He's never done anything like this to me, and the two of us have a really close and good relationship. I feel really bad for even dreaming he'd do something like that to me).

But as I was driving behind the white jeep, we eventually drive by Greensboro again. And I eventually get pissed at the car in front of me, and try to pass him at an intersection. Except, when I drive next to the man, his face is rotting. It's completely black, and you can see the flesh just starting to drip off of his skull. I think I could actually see the bone. At this point, I'm terrified, and my dad re-appears next to me and starts strangling me. Then I remember myself being thrown out of the car and hitting my head again. Then I actually woke up. I was in the same place I'd fallen asleep, and I could hear my mom calling me to get dinner.

It took me a while to make sure I was actually awake. But luckily, I am. Things make sense again. I'm pretty relieved, and I think I almost cried a couple of times. It's nighttime right now. I'm tempted to open up my bedroom blinds to make sure there's no cat staring back at me, but I'm too scared to do it. I think my dad noticed I wasn't talking to him as much as I normally do, and my entire family picked up on me acting weird. After I had dinner, I came straight to my laptop and started typing up the story. This is all I remember. If I made something up, or if I left something out, I'm really sorry. But this is everything I remember.

But that brings me to my final point: why type this out here, of all places?

I think I've been reading about/listening/writing/roleplaying/thinking about SCP a little bit too much. I have no idea if I'm overreacting or something, or if it just has to do with me being stressed and overwhelmed with school, or something else, but I just think it has something to do with me being on the SCP wiki. Has anyone here had a similar experience? Its been about two hours since I've woken up, and I haven't been able to get it off my mind. I want to be able to forget about this and dismiss it as a silly nightmare or some other crap like that, but I'm low key too terrified to even step out of my room right now. Well, with any hope, I'll be able to forget about this and move on soon. Who knows? Maybe I might even make an SCP out of this dream.
